body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students say the short vowel sound in the middle of a spoken CVC word (RF.1.2).
- Students blend three sounds into a word and segment a word into its sounds (RF.1.2).
- Students change one sound or letter in a CVC word to read and write a new word (RF.1.3).

MATERIALS
- Letter cards or magnetic letters a, e, i, o, u and common consonants
- A short vowel picture set (cat, pig, dog, bed, bus, map, sun, fish)
- Elkonin boxes (three boxes in a row) drawn on paper or a whiteboard
- Tablets with the class activity open for recording and writing

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read Sounds We Know together. Introduce tapping: one finger for each sound. Model c-a-t and s-i-t. Students tap and blend with you.
Day 2: Lesson activity: Tap and Blend. Work in small groups; students record their blends. Listen for the middle sound.
Day 3: Model changing one sound with letter cards: cat to hat, hat to hit. Students try it with partners, then start Word Builders.
Day 4: Finish Word Builders. Short vowel picture sort as a whole class: which pictures have the same middle sound?
Day 5: Assessment: Short Vowel Check. Read each word aloud twice; students write the vowel. Pull a small group for anyone who needs more time.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: use Elkonin boxes and push one counter into each box as the student says each sound. Start with short a only.
- Support: let students answer Word Builders by building the word with letter cards and taking a photo, then writing it.
- Stretch: change the middle sound as well as the first and last (cat to cut to cup). Ask students to make a word chain of five words.
- Multilingual learners: some short vowels may not exist in a student's home language. Show the mouth shape for each vowel with a mirror.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
This week your child is learning the short vowel sounds: a as in cat, e as in bed, i as in pig, o as in dog, u as in sun. Try a word game in the car or at dinner: say a word like pig, change the first sound to /b/, and ask what new word you made (big!). Thank you for practicing with us.
title: Teacher guide: Short Vowel Sounds
